passage:
A small rain shelter stood beside the road near school. It was old, and only three people could stand under it comfortably.
During a storm, many students crowded there. A tall student noticed that younger students were getting wet at the edge. He stepped into the rain and gave them space.
The next day, someone had written on the shelter wall: "Thank you to the boy who stood in the rain."
No name was written, but many students knew who it was.
The school later asked the city to build a larger shelter. Still, people remembered the small one because it had shown a quiet kind of kindness: making room for others even when it costs comfort.
